findings: No repository, code, dataset, or replay-log artifacts were supplied to this lane — only a textual description of intent (EVIDENCE.currentResearch). Claims of 'exact exchange/provider history', OKX-first continuity-checked fallbacks, and Twelve Data M5 sourcing are asserted, not demonstrated by any file, checksum, or fetch log this lane can inspect.

The 94-symbol independent per-symbol H1 family/hour/entry-geometry coordinate search is a large multiple-comparisons surface. No multiple-testing correction, no per-symbol train/validation split, and no minimum-sample-size floor is described for symbols capped at 1-3 eligible day executions — real risk that minWinRatePct=80 with RR 1:2 gets satisfied by chance for a subset of the 94 symbols rather than genuine edge.

No artifact is described that would let an outside reviewer confirm 'no silent eligible-day deletion' — e.g. a manifest of total eligible days per symbol vs. days actually included in the stats. Without that, this forbidden-list item is unverifiable from what was supplied.

'Conservative same-bar SL' is asserted but the tie-break rule for ambiguous same-bar SL/TP ordering (which level is hit first inside one H1 candle's range) is not specified — a common lookahead/leakage vector in bar-based backtests that directly affects win-rate and expectancy claims.

The 'never use FINAL for tuning' rule is stated as policy, but no technical enforcement (locked/checksummed FINAL dataset, access-controlled replay harness, separation of DEV/VALIDATION vs FINAL execution paths) is described — compliance cannot be confirmed from a policy statement alone.

Labeling V64/V69/V73 as exposed-development hypothesis-only (not OOS) is the correct bounding as stated, but no mechanism is described to prevent those legacy parameters from acting as soft priors that bias the 'independent' per-symbol search — worth an explicit check that new-search seeds/ranges were not derived from legacy winning regions.
review.proposal: Cannot issue PASS or REJECT without evidence. Before re-review: (1) supply a per-symbol data-provenance manifest for all 94 symbols (source, date range, gap/continuity-check results, fallback-trigger log); (2) specify and document the same-bar SL/TP tie-break rule and how many trades it affects; (3) supply a per-symbol eligible-day manifest (total eligible days vs. days used, with exclusion reasons) to positively rule out silent deletion; (4) document the train/validation split and any multiple-comparisons control (e.g. false-discovery correction or a held-out validation window) applied across the 94-symbol x geometry search space, since an 80% win-rate bar at this search breadth is prone to false positives; (5) show technical (not just policy) isolation of the FINAL dataset from the DEV/VALIDATION search loop, e.g. checksums or access logs. Once these artifacts are attached, this lane can perform an actual integrity audit instead of a plan-only reasoning pass.

review.proposal: Before research, freeze a machine-readable 94-symbol manifest with exact venue/provider identifiers, provenance, retrieval timestamps, raw-data hashes, timezone/session rules, and gap/duplicate/fallback continuity reports. Freeze chronological DEV, VALIDATION, and FINAL boundaries, with FINAL strictly after all legacy-prior exposure and inaccessible to tuning. Pre-register per-symbol-only geometry ranges, hour/family choices, trial budgets, deterministic tie-breaking, multiplicity controls, eligible-day logic, execution caps, transaction-cost assumptions, and full replay/event-order semantics. Permit refinements only on DEV; select once on VALIDATION without pooling or deleting symbols; lock code, data hashes, and parameters; then run FINAL exactly once. Report every symbol, eligible day, trade, exclusion reason, RR, win rate, expectancy, and invariant violation. Treat deterministic replay as the sole performance evidence.
